title: When the Visitor Sings
premise: Cyrus Crane, a property surveyor with a habit of counting doors to keep the world orderly, is hired to appraise his late grandmother's house and finds it appraising him back: every photograph in the family album now contains an extra chair, and the number of doors changes when he isn't looking. The house was built on a well that once fed a drowned village, and it refills by taking people—first as faces in photographs, then entirely. As Cyrus uncovers his grandmother's ledger of 'kept' relatives, he realizes his own name has been entered. In the end, Cyrus tricks the house into appraising itself, empties the well's count by giving the house what it truly values—the deed, the memory, and himself at the threshold—and gets his family out ahead of the final count, though he leaves behind one photograph in which he now sits in the extra chair.
about_author: M. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former land records clerk who spent years cataloguing deeds for houses no one would claim. They write horror about paperwork, inheritance, and the quiet violence of property.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Cyrus arrives at his grandmother's house to conduct its estate appraisal, keeping the lights on and counting doors out of lifelong habit—eleven doors, then twelve. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: uneasy competence curdling into dread as the professional becomes the specimen.

chapters.title: Extra Seating
chapters.summary: Sorting photographs for probate, Cyrus notices every family picture now includes an empty wooden chair that matches none in the house; his sister Dana dismisses it, but their mother goes pale and stops speaking of grandma. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the horror of evidence no one else will validate.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: In the crawlspace Cyrus finds grandmother's ledger listing names, dates, and door-counts—relatives who 'stayed,' each entry closed with a small drawn chair. The last open page bears his own name, dated next week. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as predation.

chapters.title: Doors Out of Order
chapters.summary: Dana visits to help pack; they count thirteen doors, then ten, and a hallway appears where the pantry was. Their mother, visiting briefly, hums a tune she doesn't remember learning—a song from the drowned village. POV: alternating Cyrus and Dana. Emotional beat: family solidarity strained by shared unreality.

chapters.title: What the Well Kept
chapters.summary: Cyrus researches county records: the house sits over a well that flooded a village in 1931, and every owner since has died 'in residence.' The ledger's earliest entries are the surveyor who appraised the original parcel. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the corruption of power across generations of those who measured and kept.

chapters.title: The Song Under the Floor
chapters.summary: At night the humming comes up through the floorboards; Cyrus follows it to the sealed well room and hears his mother's voice among the chorus, though she sleeps forty miles away. He nails the door shut and counts the nails aloud. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve—he refuses to be background noise.

chapters.title: Mother's Chair
chapters.summary: Their mother returns alone, drawn by the song, and is found sitting in the extra chair from the photographs, smiling, half-remembered already by her children. Cyrus drags her out; the house subtracts a door in retaliation. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: grief and guilt—the count has begun taking what they love.

chapters.title: Terms of Sale
chapters.summary: Cyrus realizes the house operates like an appraisal: it takes what it values most. He drafts a counter-offer—deed, memories, himself—but learns the well refills at dawn unless the count balances. Dana helps him forge a ledger entry closing grandma's account. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: cold clarity; turning the house's own logic against it.

chapters.title: The Count Reversed
chapters.summary: At midnight Cyrus enters the well room, reads the ledger aloud in reverse, and offers the house its own appraisal: every door, every kept face, valued and returned. The chorus falters; the chairs empty one by one; the walls begin measuring themselves. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: climax—power confronted with its own accounting.

chapters.title: Ahead of the Refill
chapters.summary: As the well roars back to full, Cyrus walks his mother and Dana out ahead of the final count, locking the front door on a house that now counts only itself. Weeks later, the new owners find one photograph with an extra chair—and a man in it, watching. POV: Dana, coda. Emotional beat: bittersweet survival; memory inherited, price paid.
